static: The Census of India is the largest statutory exercise of its kind, conducted every ten years under the Census Act of 1948.
The first synchronous census across British India was conducted in 1881 under Viceroy Lord Ripon by Sir William Plowden.

texts.x: The 1891 census was built upon foundations laid a decade earlier by the 1881 census. Its success can be attributed to a longer, more meticulous preparation period than its predecessor.

points: The second general census of India was conducted on the night of 26 February 1891 across the subcontinent.
The enumeration was led by Census Commissioner Jervoise Athelstane Baines and covered approximately 287 million persons.
The exercise built upon foundations laid by the 1881 census, benefiting from a 15-month preparation period.
Territorial coverage expanded to include Kashmir, Sikkim, Upper Burma, and certain Assam frontier tribes.
Methodological shifts included measuring livelihood support and dependents instead of just active workers.
Religion and caste data were separated into four distinct columns to reduce confusion in social analysis.
New distinctions were introduced for literacy, separating those learning under instruction from those already literate.
Persistent data collection difficulties arose with age reporting, which frequently showed preferences for multiples of five.
sum.text: O n the night of 26 February 1891, the second general census of India was conducted across the vast expanse of the subcontinent. This enumeration, which encompassed approximately 287 million persons, roughly one-fifth of the world’s estimated population at the time, represented what its Commissioner, Jervoise Athelstane Baines, rightly described as “the heaviest enterprise of the kind that has ever been undertaken.” The 1891 census was built upon foundations laid a decade earlier by the 1881 census. Its success can be attributed to a longer and more meticulous period of preparation than had been afforded to its predecessor. Acting on advice from the 1881 Commissioner, Sir William Plowden, the Government of India appointed Jervoise Athelstane Baines as Census Commissioner nearly 15 months in advance of the enumeration date. The Magnitude and Scope of the Census The scale of the 1891 census challenges comprehension even by contemporary standards. The final returns enumerated 287,223,431 persons. Show Full Article To place this number in perspective, Baines observed that the population of Bengal alone “has an area equal to that of the United Kingdom, with the addition of a second Scotland, whilst the population is about that of the whole of the United States of America in 1890, together with that of Mexico (Baines, 1893).” The territorial coverage of the 1891 census was expanded from its predecessor. The new census brought within its scope Kashmir, Sikkim, Upper Burma, and a portion of the frontier tribes in Assam and the far east, the areas which were excluded from the 1881 exercise. These additions substantially added to the population under enumeration (Baines, 1893). However, certain tracts remained excluded: Nepal and Bhutan were not included, nor were the border tribes of Balochistan or the coastal settlements dependent on Aden. The small state of Sikkim was enumerated only informally, with its population excluded from the general returns. The complete enumeration encompassed both British territory and feudatory states. British territory comprised 62 percent of the area but 77 percent of the population, while the feudatory states contained 38 percent of the area but only 23 percent of the population. This disparity was due to the inclusion within the states of extensive wild tracts, desert portions of the Indus valley, and forest-covered hills of the central belt: regions where population density remained low (Baines, 1893). points: Traditional cybersecurity relies on firewalls, patching, and training, but artificial intelligence is now reducing the time, cost, and expertise needed to discover and exploit weaknesses.
The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities exposed over 22.6 million internet-facing systems worldwide to potential remote attacks, highlighting severe risks to global digital infrastructure.
PHP2Shell involves two critical vulnerabilities with a severity rating of 9.2 out of 10, allowing attackers to execute malicious code remotely without logging in.
AI models assisted in vulnerability discovery through programmes like OpenAI's Patch the Planet and collaboration with Anthropic, demonstrating AI's dual-use potential for both defense and offense.
Legacy systems running older PHP versions face severe exposure because official fixes are unavailable, and patching across affected systems could continue until 2027.
India's major Digital Public Infrastructure platforms like Aadhaar, GSTN, UPI, and MCA21 reportedly operate on other technology stacks, but interconnected systems remain vulnerable.
Attackers hold an inherent advantage because they need only one exploitable weakness, while defenders must secure thousands of interconnected applications and interfaces.
Organisations must adopt an assume-breach approach, prioritize patching and mitigation, strengthen network-level detection, and improve board-level cybersecurity oversight.
sum.text:
Cybersecurity has relied on measures such as firewalls, timely patching and employee training to prevent attacks. However, artificial intelligence (AI) is reducing the time, cost and expertise required to discover and exploit weaknesses. The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities exposed millions of internet-facing systems to potential remote attacks, highlighting risks to digital infrastructure. The incident raises questions about AI’s dual-use potential, India’s preparedness and the need to strengthen cyber resilience.
Meaning of PHP: PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a free, open-source scripting language that processes website functions such as logins, application submissions and online purchases.
Origin: PHP originated as Personal Home Page Tools and was created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1994. Its source code was publicly released in 1995.
Management: The PHP Foundation supports development and maintenance, but does not control PHP language decisions. Those remain with the PHP Internals community through its RFC (Request for Comments) process.
Global Dependence: Around 70% of websites with identifiable server-side languages use PHP, making its vulnerabilities a widespread concern. WordPress, which powers over 40% of websites globally, also uses PHP.
PHP2Shell: PHP2Shell refers to two critical vulnerabilities in PHP that could allow attackers to execute malicious code on affected web servers remotely without logging in.
◦ Memory problem: When an error interrupts a process, PHP may treat incomplete information as valid, creating a security weakness.
◦ Leftover information: PHP may use information left from an earlier request while processing a new request , causing incorrect handling .
Severity and Exposure: The vulnerabilities received a severity rating of 9.2/10 . Over 22.6 million internet-exposed instances worldwide could be vulnerable.
Potential Risks: Attackers could install malware , remove website content, access sensitive information , including passwords and login credentials, and disrupt server operations .
Security Fixes: The PHP Foundation released security patches and urged immediate installation . If affected systems cannot be secured promptly, cyber agencies advise temporarily taking websites offline .
Difficulty of Fixing: Small website owners, shared hosting users and older systems may struggle to identify PHP installations and apply updates . Compatibility, performance and third-party extensions can further complicate upgrades .

texts.x: India must adapt to a US relationship driven by pragmatic deal-making, rethink its diaspora policy amid anti-immigrant sentiment, and play a bigger role in easing Iran tensions and shaping the global order.

points: The India-US strategic partnership has shifted toward pragmatic deal-making, with US officials engaging heavily with Indian corporate leaders on energy and infrastructure.
India needs to factor three key developments into its foreign policy: strategic dhandha, a rethink of diaspora policy, and looming geopolitical tensions surrounding Iran.
The era of long-term strategic alignment is replaced by flexible, transactional engagement, as demonstrated by Marco Rubio's meetings with Indian corporate bosses.
India avoided Russia tariffs due to White House recognition of Indian refineries, while an upcoming trade deal awaits reconciliation on tariffs and the US trade deficit.
India is due to sign trade deals with Canada and the European Union in December, giving it leverage in its ongoing negotiations with the United States.
India must differentiate between anti-immigrant MAGA sentiment targeting India and that targeting Indian-American citizens, focusing its diplomatic efforts on protecting Indian citizens abroad.
Anticipated US midterm reverses may free Donald Trump to take a maximalist approach on Iran, raising risks of regional conflict affecting energy and submarine infrastructure.
With a potential Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting approaching in Shenzhen, India needs to play a proactive role in the Quad to help shape the future global order.
sum.text: The only sign the India-US relationship retains vestiges of a strategic partnership was when Marco Rubio paid tribute at the 26/11 memorial at Mumbai's Taj Mahal Palace. The official US reaffirmation of India's position on post-9/11, post-26/11 cross-border terrorism could be the one bright spot in an otherwise gloomy relationship at a time when Donald Trump's lovefest with Asim Munir is obvious. India needs to factor 3 developments into its foreign policy: Strategic dhandha For a quarter of a century, the US assumed a 'strategic, long-term' view of India. That period is decisively over. India is now smack in the middle of the age of pragmatic deal-making, or 'dhandha' as strategy. That is fine, if Indians realise the field is flexible, with spin, seam and yorkers all being bowled in the same over. Field placement is, therefore, more important than ever, since India cannot afford not to engage with this new phase of the US. Rubio's meeting with the Ambanis was more animated than his meetings with (Indian and UAE) foreign ministers. The former was about buying Venezuelan oil and a refinery in Texas. The latter ticked boxes, including I2U2 and IMEC, both currently hostage to the Iran war. Rubio met Mukesh Ambani, Gautam Adani and N Chandrasekaran (almost 15 Indian corporate bosses had reportedly sought a meeting). It says one important thing: despite turbulence, both countries continue to find reasons to make money together. Energy, infrastructure, defence and technology are touchpoints of the India-US corridor, a good reason for Rubio to have spent time in India twice in 4 months. India was saved from Russia tariffs for two reasons: someone in the White House decided that Indian oil refineries are a force for good in the world, and that an India trade deal might be a good idea. Leverage is everything. The trade deal will be 'done' when two things are reconciled - certainty on India tariffs and a roadmap to reduce the US trade deficit. Meanwhile, India is due to sign trade deals with Canada and the EU in December. So, it can afford to wait for a favourable landing point with the US. Modi will be in Canada, US, and EU in December - 2 out of 3 trade deals would be an acceptable record. It's a good way to deal with the US, and India is proving to be a quick learner. Rethink diaspora policy For future stability of its US relationship, India needs to rethink its diaspora policy, beyond the previous pomp. Whether it's Trump-Vance Republicans, or Socialist…

sum.text:
India has digitally surveyed more than 31.3 crore agricultural plots, yet a far bigger economic opportunity remains largely untapped: Turning farm data into finance for measurable climate outcomes. Knowing what grows where is useful, but can India also reward farmers for conserving water, reducing emissions, improving soil health and building climate resilience? The next agricultural digital revolution should not be another app or registry.
It should be an infrastructure that makes these outcomes easier to measure, credible to verify and economically viable to finance. The foundations are already substantial. During Rabi 2025–26, the Digital Crop Survey covered more than 31.3 crore plots across 648 districts, while over 10.33 crore Farmer IDs had been generated by August 6, 2026.
These figures reflect expanding digital coverage, not farmers already accessing climate finance. Backed by the ₹2,817 crore Digital Agriculture Mission, AgriStack is developing farmer, crop and village-map registries, while the separate Krishi Decision Support System integrates geospatial, weather, crop and water data. This matters because agriculture faces a financing problem that is, in part, a measurement problem. A solar plant has a defined asset and metered output. Across dispersed farms, a lender or carbon buyer must establish which practices changed, whether an outcome followed and how long it lasted.

Ukraine said on Saturday that Starlink and its military version, Starshield, had returned to normal operating speeds after more than a week of restrictions that disrupted military operations. Hours later, Elon Musk, who owns the satellite systems, accused the Ukrainian military of violating their terms of service by using them for offensive drone attacks.
"Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," Musk said in a post on X. Ukrainian officials did not immediately respond publicly to the allegation.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the systems had resumed operating at the speeds Ukraine needed. The restrictions, which capped speeds at 160 kph, had hampered efforts to intercept Russian attack drones and forced the cancellation of some military operations.
"The main thing for today is that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need," he said on the Telegram app.
Starlink is crucial to Ukrainian frontline communications, while Starshield-enabled medium-range attack drones have helped Kyiv gain ground in several areas this year. Ukraine, however, does not rely on the systems for long-range drone attacks on Russian territory, including strikes on oil refineries.
The restrictions also coincided with disruptions to allied warnings about incoming Russian missile attacks, sparking anger in Kyiv. Ukraine later said it continued to receive US intelligence.
Neither Musk nor the US government has publicly acknowledged responsibility for the restrictions, with both indicating that the other could have ordered them. Reuters has reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from within the White House.
The dispute unfolded amid broader tensions over US policy towards the war. The restrictions followed President Donald Trump's announcement of a deal to buy Russian diesel while pressing Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries.

sum.text:
India's 75th Ramsar site was announced with the kind of fanfare that accompanies a record broken. What followed the announcement, in most cases, was silence, not because nothing was required, but because the requirements are poorly understood outside the small circle of wetland ecologists who track them.
The Ramsar Convention Is a Framework, Not a Rulebook India ratified the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance in 1982. The treaty, signed in the Iranian city of Ramsar in 1971, does not create a supranational authority with enforcement powers. It operates on the principle of wise use, a term the convention defines as the maintenance of ecological character through the implementation of ecosystem approaches. What that means in practice is that the obligation sits entirely with the member state. No Ramsar secretariat officer arrives to inspect a site. No penalty clause triggers if a listed wetland shrinks. The pressure is reputational, diplomatic, and, increasingly, legal, because India's own courts have begun citing Ramsar obligations in wetland protection cases.
The Montreux Record and What Triggers It Once a wetland is listed, the host country is required to inform the Ramsar Secretariat if the ecological character of the site has changed, is changing, or is likely to change as a result of human interference. Sites where this has happened can be placed on the Montreux Record, a register of Ramsar sites under threat. Loktak Lake in Manipur, home to the only floating national park in the world and the habitat of the endangered Sangai deer, has been on the Montreux Record since 1993. Being on the record is not a punishment; it is a formal request for assistance and attention. But it is also an acknowledgment that the listing did not protect the site. Loktak's problems, encroachment, weed infestation, siltation from the Ithai Barrage, predate its Ramsar status and have outlasted three decades of it.
The Management Plan Requirement Every Ramsar site is expected to have a management plan that integrates it into land-use planning at the local and national level. In India, this responsibility falls to the state government in whose territory the wetland sits, coordinated through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, require a wetland authority for each notified wetland and a management plan prepared by that authority. The study, Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends, developed a quarterly framework to track economic activity in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka using indicators that are available more frequently than official state economic data. The combined indicators also improved estimates compared with using satellite data alone. The study found a strong correlation between year-on-year growth in night-time lights and overall GSVA growth. The correlation was highest in Maharashtra at 0.90, followed by Karnataka at 0.79 and Gujarat at 0.66. The relationship remained strong and statistically significant even after the researchers excluded quarters affected by the Covid-19 pandemic. Night-time light data also provided predictive information about subsequent GSVA growth, while Google Trends data appeared to contribute mainly through contemporaneous signals. The researchers cautioned that the framework had been tested only in three industrial states. They said it was intended to complement, rather than replace, official economic statistics.
